cases.evidence: Rendered screenshot (probe --shot) shows a dashed line labelled 'Quota 3.0M' spanning the plot and a white bold value label inside every bar (3.1M / 2.6M / 2.2M / 3.4M); Fred's and Bob's bar tops sit visibly below the dashed line. SVG source confirms: `<line ... y1='105' y2='105' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/>` + `<text ...>Quota 3.0M</text>` + per-bar value <text> nodes. The alt itself also states 'The yearly quota is 3.0 million dollars and is shown as a dashed line' in addition to all four figures. Corpus mechanism asserts below-quota membership 'exists only as the red fill ... reaching neither AT nor colour-blind sighted users'.
cases.reasoning: Ajit's factual premise is verified: position-vs-quota-line plus numeric labels are genuine non-colour visual cues, so the mechanism's claim that colour-blind sighted users cannot resolve who is below quota is false as shipped. Whether that flips the verdict is a real judgment call: the page is otherwise a verbatim reproduction of the F13 example (same four names and figures), and F13 says such an alt fails 1.1.1 AND 1.4.1 because it never names who missed quota — though this alt, unlike F13's, also supplies the 3.0M quota so the fact is derivable arithmetically. Resolving this changes `expected`, so it is not FIX-OBVIOUS; a human must decide between (a) keep failed and rewrite the mechanism to drop the 'colour-blind sighted users' claim, or (b) flip to passed / strip the quota line and value labels to restore the canonical F13 conditions.

cases.evidence: probe-case.js --click '#open-search' --key Escape: click.focusAfter = input#q ('Search The Meridian'); afterKey.focus = {tag:'body'} — focus is NOT on #q and NOT on #open-search after Escape. Tab walk from load: stop 1 = button#open-search (aria-label 'Open search'), stop 2 = Subscribe, then the nav links — #open-search IS the first focusable control in the page. Source lines 104-108: closeSearch() removes .open and sets aria-hidden=true with no openBtn.focus().
cases.reasoning: Ajit's complaint is refuted on both limbs: focus does not return to #open-search (it falls to document.body when the container goes display:none), and #open-search genuinely is the first focusable stop (the masthead 'logo' is a non-focusable <span> and the nav links come later in DOM). The F85 failure is real and expected=failed stands — F85's own example is exactly 'focus is set to the document. The user must tab from the beginning'. However the case's own scenario/mechanism state something the browser plainly contradicts ('focus stranded on the now-hidden input', 'activeElement is #q with a 0x0 box'); that string is mechanically fixable and does not touch `expected`.

proposedFix.rationale: Correct the two prose claims that Chromium contradicts (verified by probe: activeElement is BODY after Escape, not #q). The failure and the label are unchanged — F85 explicitly covers the focus-goes-to-document case, and the 'next Tab restarts at #open-search' claim was verified true. The .md (eval/act-augmented/2.4.3/pages/f85-focus-return-after-dismissal/case-04.md) already says focus 'falls back toward the document/body' but reportedly carries a loose 'focus is left on a hidden node' clause — it should get the same wording sweep.

edits.newString: leaving focus unrestored (Chromium blurs the now-hidden input, so focus reverts to the document body) and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page.

edits.oldString: focus lingers on #q inside a hidden subtree. Verified by Puppeteer: after Escape, activeElement is #q with a 0x0 box inside a display:none container, and the next Tab moves to #open-search

cases.evidence: probe-case.js --hover 'abbr.gloss': the .bub tooltip becomes visible on hover (text 'Gross Domestic Product — ...', rect 208x71), then hoverableAfterPointerTravel=false — moving the pointer into the bubble makes it disappear; visibleTooltipsAfterEscape=0 (it was already gone). Source explains why: `.gloss > .bub { ... pointer-events:none; }` (line 34) and show/hide bound only to mouseenter/mouseleave/focus/blur on the abbr (lines 85-88), with the bubble rendered above the trigger (bottom:1.6em), so leaving the trigger box hides it.
cases.reasoning: Davin says 'It is hoverable, but not escapable. Not both.' The probe shows the opposite on the hoverable limb: because the bubble is pointer-events:none and the mouseleave handler sits on the trigger, the pointer cannot travel onto the additional content without it vanishing — an F95-style hoverable failure. Dismissible also fails (no Escape handler at all), so the case fails on two limbs, not one, and expected=failed is unaffected either way since 1.4.13 requires all applicable limbs.

cases.evidence: case-01.html lines 47-52 render every amount with an explicit sign ('+$2,410.00' credits, '−$6.75' debits) and the page footer (lines 57-58) says 'Money in is shown in green and includes a leading plus sign; money out is shown in dark red with a leading minus sign.' The result.json scenario/mechanism/whyAutomatedToolsMiss — the fields the annotator UI shows (index.html lines 523-524, 1255) — mention only the 3.15:1 inter-foreground lightness ratio. The .md doc, which annotators do NOT see, already says '(Standard +/- signs are also present.)' and '(The +/- signs are a further non-colour cue, but the escape hatch alone governs the verdict.)'. I recomputed the colours: L(#3a9d4e)=0.2556, L(#7a1414)=0.0469 → 3.155:1; green/white 3.44:1, red/white 10.84:1 — the corpus numbers are accurate.
cases.reasoning: Ajit is right about what he was shown: the served rationale omits the page's most obvious non-colour cue and presents the case as if the lightness escape hatch alone carried the PASS. The label is not in play — the page passes 1.4.1 twice over — so the repair is a prose sync that copies the author's own already-written parenthetical from the .md into the served metadata. The alternative repair (deleting the +/- signs to isolate the escape hatch) would change the page and is a corpus-design decision, not a mechanical one; the patch below deliberately only adds true statements.

proposedFix.rationale: Sync the served mechanism prose with the shipped page (and with the case's own .md, which already documents the +/- signs). Only adds a true statement; expected stays 'passed'. No .md change needed — eval/act-augmented/1.4.1/pages/scoping-non-failures-and-escape-hatches/case-01.md lines 4 and 22 already say this. manifest.json must be regenerated from result.json afterwards.

edits.oldString: Each colour also meets SC 1.4.3 against white (green 3.44:1 as large-bold text, red 10.84:1), so contrast minimums are not the issue.
edits.newString: Each colour also meets SC 1.4.3 against white (green 3.44:1 as large-bold text, red 10.84:1), so contrast minimums are not the issue. The amounts additionally carry leading +/- signs (and the footer states both cues), so the PASS is over-determined — the lightness escape hatch is what this case is about, but it is not the page's only non-colour cue.

edits.oldString: Why this PASSES (and why it is the boundary control): The snackbar <div id="snackbar" role="status" aria-live="polite"> is present in the markup at page load as an empty, registered live region. Adding to cart writes ONLY textContent into that pre-existing region (“Yirgacheffe added to your cart. 1 item.”) and toggles a CSS class to slide it in. Because the region existed and was empty when the AT registered it, the later text mutation IS announced. This is the correct ARIA19/ARIA22 step-1 pattern and the exact opposite of the born-with-content failures in case-01 through case-05 — same final markup, but the region pre-existed the message. The marker data-region-preexisting-empty="true" records the correct timing.
